subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: Which candidate should own the canonical fix for critical tool-loop termination, and is deferring queued steering/follow-up input to a fresh prompt the intended session contract?
rationale: Both open PRs implement nearly identical runtime behavior, while the queue-delivery consequence is a user-visible session-state choice that tests and synthetic proof cannot authorize.

options.title: Repair and prove this PR
options.body: Fix the missing type import, rebase onto current main, add real session proof for termination and queued-input recovery, and close the competing PR after this one is selected.

options.title: Adopt the competing PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106297 as the landing candidate only after it supplies equivalent real behavior proof and current-main compatibility.

options.title: Replace both candidates
options.body: Pause both PRs and implement the same dual-layer contract in an owner-authored branch if neither branch cleanly survives the current agent-runtime refactor.

recommendation.title: Repair and prove this PR
recommendation.body: Fix the missing type import, rebase onto current main, add real session proof for termination and queued-input recovery, and close the competing PR after this one is selected.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places this owner closest to the agent-session and tool-execution boundary where the queue and terminal-state contract must be chosen.
